_README: Anthropic published list prices for the three models this pipeline uses, plus a skeleton for the
Azure/OpenAI models. See configs/model_pricing.example.json for what each key means and how a
missing rate degrades.
A cache WRITE is the only class whose rate depends on how long the entry is asked to live, so
both columns are carried here:
cache_write_5m   1.25x `in` — a 5-minute entry, what a bare cache_control asks for
cache_write_1h   2x `in`    — a 1-hour entry, what cache_control with ttl "1h" asks for
extractor/pricing.py prices whichever column matches MODEL_CACHE_TTL for the run (1h by default)
and names the choice as `cache_ttl` in the cost block. So flipping that variable reprices the
run on its own — do not collapse these two keys back into one `cache_write`.
The `models` section is keyed by the exact model id a run records, and it wins over `tiers`. It is
there because a tier name says how important a call was, not what it cost: `high` is claude-opus-5
on --provider ica and a gpt-5 model on --provider azure. The `tiers` section below stays as the
fallback for a Claude run and for any model with no entry of its own.
The GPT-5.6 entries use the supplied deployment price table. The four values are stored as
new input, cached input, cache write, and output rates, respectively. The supplied table does
not distinguish cache-write lifetime, so each uses the single `cache_write` rate for either
configured TTL. These are estimates until the gateway publishes a deployment-specific rate card.
The model keys must match whatever the run resolves. On azure that is AZURE_MODEL_<TIER> in .env,
falling back to _TIER_DEFAULTS in extractor/llm.py. Rename these
keys if your deployment uses different ids, or the tier rates get used instead and the cost block
reports rates_basis 'tier'.
These are vendor list prices, NOT a gateway contract. Calls go through the IBM ICA gateway (ica) or
an Azure OpenAI deployment (azure), either of which may bill differently. Treat the run's
`total_usd` as an estimate at list price.
